=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py:59 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The CI lint job fails with AssertionError: Unclassified checkout@v5 workflows: ['integration-pr-readiness.yml', 'lint-plan-archival.yml', 'lint-pr-body-auto-close.yml']. The three new workflow files added by this PR all use actions/checkout@v5 but none appear in ALLOWLIST_EXCEPTIONS or REQUIRED_RESOLVER_WORKFLOWS in the audit test.
  WHY: The audit test enumerates all .github/workflows/*.yml files containing 'uses: actions/checkout@v5', then asserts every such file is classified. All three new workflows use checkout@v5, none are classified, so test_checkout_workflows_are_all_classified() raises AssertionError. This blocks the lint job on every push to this PR, as confirmed by the PR check runs context showing failed[0].name=lint with conclusion=failure and the log tail containing the exact AssertionError.
- .github/workflows/mark-stable.yml and .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The three new test files (tests/test_lint_pr_body_auto_close.py, tests/test_lint_plan_archival_completeness.py, tests/test_check_integration_pr_readiness.py) are added to .github/workflows/ci.yml but are absent from both release/stable workflow unit-test allowlists. These workflows use explicit python3 tests/<file>.py invocations with no discovery mechanism.
  WHY: When the mark-stable release pipeline runs, the new lint enforcement contracts (P1 auto-close keyword check, P3 integration-PR readiness check, P6 plan-archival completeness check) will not be tested against the stable branch. A regression in any of these lint scripts that passes CI on a PR branch can ship to stable without detection. grep confirms zero matches across both stable workflow files while ci.yml has 3 matches.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The completeness gate writes a new `external_finalize_partial_alert_sig` value to the state file using a `STATE_FILE.tmp` + `mv` pattern that is atomic at the filesystem level, but the preceding read of `_orch_extfin_prev_sig` from the same STATE_FILE and the jq modification that produces STATE_FILE.tmp are not protected by any lock or synchronization primitive.
  WHY: If two concurrent poll ticks both enter the external-finalize block for the same tracking issue before either persists the signature, both compute the same missing-set signature, both find it different from the previous (still-empty) signature, and both fire tg_notify. The second tick's mv overwrites the first tick's identical signature — no state corruption, but the dedup fails and the operator receives two identical WARNING Telegram alerts instead of one. The orchestrator's concurrency group configuration may prevent true parallel runs in practice, but the code has no self-protection if that guarantee is ever weakened.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When cp "${merge_tmpdir}/int" "${f}" fails after a successful git merge-file, the function emits a warning and moves on without staging the file. The merge result in the tmpdir is discarded, the integration-branch file remains unchanged, and the refresh intent is silently dropped.
  WHY: A transient filesystem error (ENOSPC, EIO, permission change) on the worktree file causes the 3-way merge result to be lost. The function does not retry, does not escalate, and does not leave any persistent signal beyond the stderr warning. The orchestrator continues to the next poll tick under the assumption the file was refreshed, but the toolchain fix from main never reached the integration branch — recreating the exact class of problem (main-side fix not propagating) that P5 was designed to prevent. The original PR's code had this same gap; the LAST RUN DIFF hardened the git cat-file materialization and git add failure paths but left the cp failure path unchanged.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
